content.text: Chronic inflammation is at the root of most modern diseases — from heart disease to autoimmune conditions. The foods you eat every day can either fuel that inflammation or fight it. These seven recipes are built around the most powerful anti-inflammatory ingredients available.

items: Turmeric — contains curcumin, one of the most studied anti-inflammatory compounds
Ginger — blocks prostaglandins that trigger inflammation
Salmon & fatty fish — omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA) reduce inflammatory markers
Leafy greens — vitamin K and polyphenols reduce NF-kB signaling
Extra virgin olive oil — oleocanthal has similar effects to ibuprofen

content.text: Combine 1 cup red lentils, 1 can coconut milk, 2 cups vegetable broth, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, fresh ginger, and garlic. Simmer 20 minutes until lentils are soft. This one pot wonder delivers fiber, plant protein, and a potent dose of curcumin.
Always pair turmeric with black pepper — piperine in pepper increases curcumin absorption by up to 2000%.

items.question: What foods should I avoid to reduce inflammation?
items.answer: Limit refined sugars, processed vegetable oils (soybean, corn), refined grains, processed meats, and excess alcohol — these are the primary dietary drivers of inflammation.

items.question: How quickly do anti-inflammatory foods work?
items.answer: Some people notice reduced bloating and improved energy within 3–5 days of consistent anti-inflammatory eating. Full systemic benefits typically appear after 4–8 weeks.
